entities.summary:
Heraklas was a Greek physician of the 1st century AD whose descriptions of surgeons' knots and slings are preserved in book 48 of Oribasius' Medical Collections under the title From Heraklas.

As a key figure in the development of medical knowledge, Heraklas contributed to the understanding of surgical techniques and patient care.

His work had a lasting impact on the field of medicine, particularly in the areas of surgery and anesthesia.

The Medical Collections, which date back to the 3rd century AD, contain Heraklas' writings on various medical topics, including surgery, pharmacology, and diagnosis.

The title 'From Heraklas' is a testament to the enduring significance of his work in the medical community.

The fact that his descriptions of surgeons' knots and slings are still referenced in modern medical texts over two millennia later is a striking example of the lasting legacy of Heraklas.

Heraklas' work not only advanced medical knowledge but also had a profound impact on the development of medical education and practice.

In conclusion, Heraklas' contributions to medicine were significant, far-reaching, and continue to influence medical practice today.
